judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Plain and Jandor-like, but the reminder reads like a tooltip pasted into speech ('Haste will be invaluable', 'turn aside their clubs'), and the opening leans on two 'But' sentences in a row.

items.label: B
items.critique: The exclamations fit, but every sentence gets one, and 'leaving the broken bridge our smallest worry' and 'the whole north road is in peril' are built-up stakes Westwood's briefings rarely spell out.

items.label: C
items.critique: Clipped arrival, fragment exclamations, the double-dash aside and a dry closing jab ('It weeds out the weak recruits'): this is the campaign's voice.

items.label: D
items.critique: 'The long road has tested your mettle well' is stock fantasy, and the logic is spelled out ('most certainly behind it all'); the reminder adds a chatty aside ('He wants a word with you').

items.label: E
items.critique: Short pages, a practical airship drop-off and a gruff reminder are true to Nox; 'Forest beasts will heed its bite' is the only slightly ornate turn.

items.label: F
items.critique: Organised like a modern quest brief (go here, find this title, take the lamp and gold, visit the shop, take the lift) with careful logistics; 'I've nothing more to say to you' sounds like a writer's idea of gruff.

items.label: G
items.critique: The 'brave Adventurer' greeting and the imp-like mischief are close to Nox, but the offer piles up exposition and directions ('in my hall at the heart of the college'), and the reminder is flavour, not a push.

items.label: H
items.critique: A terse drop-off, 'You remain our only hope', 'No more time for chit-chat', and a long, clunky journal line that is very much Westwood's.

items.label: I
items.critique: Very terse fragments ('You'll know. And careful.') and a reminder that repeats the order nearly word for word: the slightly rough redundancy of the shipped game.

items.label: J
items.critique: Odd grammar ('The Master for the [Place]' as a fragment, 'convey the [Thing]') and the capitalised 'YOU' are the campaign's quirks; no generated text would be this stiff on purpose.

tells: Westwood's briefings are terse and a little rough: sentence fragments, repeated orders in the reminder, odd word choices and plain clunky journal lines. The new texts are smoother and better organised.
New texts spell out stakes and reasoning ('the whole north road is in peril', 'most certainly behind it all') where Westwood just gives the order and an exclamation.
New texts give step-by-step logistics in the offer (title of the contact, item handed over, shop, lift, where to report back), like a modern quest brief.
Stock fantasy idioms ('tested your mettle', 'turn aside their clubs', 'heed its bite') mark the new texts; Westwood's colour is drier and shorter ('It weeds out the weak recruits').
New reminders tend to be flavour or attitude lines ('I've nothing more to say to you', 'making too much mischief lately'); Westwood's simply repeat the push to go now.
